subject: Discovery recap: model fit, eval plan & quantization tradeoffs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: model fit, eval plan & quantization tradeoffs

Thanks again for taking the call today, Alex — good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan.

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use: customer support triage + contextual summarization for agents (short contexts, often multi-turn).
- Latency requirement: targeting p50 < 200ms and p95 < 450ms for 1-2k QPS peaks.
- Monthly volume: roughly ~50M tokens today (est).
- Security: data residency in US, standard SOC2 controls needed.

Recommended short list for eval (initial):
1) Llama-3-Chat-34B-8k (baseline; strong instruction following)
2) Mistral-Instruct-70B (high quality for long instructions)
3) Vicuna-13B / small 70B variants for low-latency tiers

Quantization & throughput tradeoffs to validate
- AWQ (8-bit asymmetric): best throughput improvement for decoder workloads with minimal single-token quality impact in many workloads; good for production throughput.
- GPTQ (4/3-bit style): typically better model-size reduction and lower memory, but more engineering work and can introduce more variability on instruction-following unless tuned.
- FP8 (hardware-dependent): promising latency wins on newer HW but quality/compatibility varies; treat as experimental.

Attachments I shared:
- finwave_eval_promptset_v1.txt (prompt set we discussed - short representative conversations + edge cases)
- redwood_awq_gptq_fp8_tradeoffs.pdf (short trade study summary)

Next steps
- We'll upload a small eval run against the prompt set and share benchmark links by EOD tomorrow.
- Can you confirm: (1) procurement contact to loop in for PoC contracting, and (2) any additional compliance docs needed (besides SOC2)?
- Proposed next meeting: Thurs 7/22 to review benchmarks & pick PoC model/quantization path.

If that all sounds right I'll kick off the scoped eval and run AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 baselines and share a dashboard.

Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa - helpful summary. A couple clarifications from our side:

1) Latency: 200ms p50 is a soft target; p95 450ms is the hard limit for UI interactions. For async agent workflows we can tolerate higher p95 but prefer throughput wins.
2) Token volume: 50M/month is our current estimate; we have a roadmap to double in 6-9 months.
3) Compliance: SOC2 is required; we also need to confirm data retention and logging options (audit logs for 12 months).

Procurement loop-in is procurement@finwave.com (I've cc'd). John Lee (cc'd) is our platform lead and will want the benchmark artifacts.

Happy to meet Thurs 7/22 10am PT if that works for you and Rishi.

Appreciate the details, Alex - confirmed Thurs 7/22 10am PT works for us. I pushed a small eval run and initial bench results to the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-eval-artifacts and a lightweight dashboard at https://notebooks.redwood.com/finwave/eval-run-20270720.

Short summary of what we found in the initial 500-sample run (prompt set attached):
- AWQ on Llama-3-Chat-34B: ~2.6x token throughput improvement vs fp16 baseline on our A100 pool, measured p50 latency ~180ms at 40QPS with slightly elevated p95 (~420ms). Quality delta vs fp16: negligible on majority of user-facing metrics; a handful of instruction edge cases show minor regressions.
- GPTQ (4-bit) on Llama-3-Chat-34B: ~3.8x memory reduction, throughput similar to AWQ once kernel fusion is tuned; quality retention was slightly better on creative/long-form outputs but required extra quantization calibration.
- FP8 (experimental HW): showed best single-token latency on Ampere-NGPUs with vendor FP8 kernels, but results are hardware-dependent and we recommend it as a later-stage optimization for specific fleets.

Recommendation for PoC path (minimal risk + clear validation):
1) Start with Llama-3-Chat-34B quantized with AWQ (fast to deploy, good throughput/quality balance).
2) Parallel GPTQ run on a small subset to validate any edge-case regressions (if quality-sensitive flows need it, we can flip to GPTQ variants).
3) Keep FP8 as experimental; evaluate later once we lock model and infra.

I attached the trade study and the CSV of the microbenchmarks (benchmarks_awq_gptq_fp8.csv). That includes token-level latency distributions, quality buckets (pass/fail by prompt), and cost-per-1M-token estimates for each path.

Ballpark cost delta (example sizing for 50M tokens/month):
- fp16 baseline: $X (baseline reference)
- AWQ deployment: ~25-35% lower unit cost vs fp16 depending on batching and caching
- GPTQ deployment: ~30-45% lower unit cost vs fp16 on typical workloads once tuned
Note: these are engineering-estimate ranges; we'll pin numbers in the PoC.

Next steps
- Confirm procurement contact & start a standard PoC SOW (I've cc'd procurement).
- We'll schedule Thurs 7/22 10am PT (invite to follow).
- Redwood to run a 2-week PoC: AWQ production-like run + a parallel GPTQ quality validation for a prioritized subset.

If that looks good I'll also share the prompt-level regression report before the meeting.

Marissa Cole
